clue.text: Surprise fat pig eating middle of burger

parts.note: flab is body fat

indicators.note: the pig takes the next letters inside it, as if eating them

parts.note: a beast is a brutish person, a pig

indicators.note: the central pair of letters of the six-letter word burger

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked to see a fat pig tucking into the middle of a burger.
explanation.walkthrough: Pig here is a beast, not a hog or swine; 'middle of' takes the central pair of burger's six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish someone utterly is to take them completely by surprise; both are verbs.

clue.text: Pack animal's hit bearing load unevenly

indicators.note: the odd letters carry the next piece between them, bearing it
the uneven-numbered, i.e. odd, letters of load are taken

parts.note: to lam is to hit or thrash

explanation.surface: A beast of burden takes a knock from a badly balanced load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unevenly' means the odd-numbered letters, first and third, which 'bearing' wraps round the word for hit.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American camelid is widely kept as a beast of burden in the Andes.

clue.text: Live round's opening, puncturing strike explosive

indicators.note: the letter pierces the word for strike, going inside it

parts.note: to strike is to beat

indicators.note: the opening letter of round is its first

parts.note: HE is short for high explosive

explanation.surface: A live round's first shot pierces something about to blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: Live reads as an adjective about ammunition, but it is the verb, to be alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing breath is the basic sign of being alive, so to breathe is to live.

clue.text: Former wife's audibly kissed on demand

parts.note: an ex is a former wife

indicators.note: the word for kissed is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: pecked means kissed lightly

explanation.surface: An ex-wife is said to have been kissed on request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audibly' turns PECKED into the sound PECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To require something of someone as their duty, as in 'I expect better', is to demand it.

clue.text: Challenged Government while accepting popular funding

indicators.note: the word for while takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: as can mean while
in means popular, fashionable
aid is financial help, funding

explanation.surface: Ministers face a challenge for taking a fashionable kind of financial support.
explanation.walkthrough: Challenged means disputed or contradicted here, not tested; 'accepting' wraps the word for while round popular.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny or contradict a claim is to dispute it, so the past tense matches challenged.

clue.text: This may help with clinical depression?

definitions.text: This may help with clinical depression?

parts.words: This may help with clinical depression?
parts.note: a doctor's flat blade presses the tongue down for an examination, a literal depression in a clinic

explanation.surface: A question about what might relieve serious depression.
explanation.walkthrough: Clinical depression sounds like mental illness, but it is a doctor pressing the tongue down to look at the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue depressor is a flat instrument used by clinicians to hold the tongue down.

clue.text: Panic seeing rook, queen and knight in position

parts.note: to rook is to swindle, to con

indicators.note: the queen and knight go inside the word for position

parts.note: a station is a post or position
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A chess player panics on seeing rook, queen and knight placed in a certain position.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess pieces mislead: rook is a verb meaning con, not R. 'in' puts ERN inside STATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay and alarm amounting to panic; both are nouns for sudden fright.

clue.text: Mortarboard?

parts.note: an academic cap is something worn on the head, and also the kind of thing a head teacher might wear

explanation.surface: A one-word question about a graduation cap.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: a mortarboard is one kind of hat, and suggests what a head might wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortarboard is a square academic cap, one example of things worn on the head.

clue.text: Lanky unknown boxes heartlessly, waves as usual

indicators.note: the tall unknown encloses the next piece, as in a box

parts.note: lanky means tall

indicators.note: the central letter of the word for waves is removed

parts.note: radiation travels as waves
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A lanky stranger is boxing without heart and waving as he always does.
explanation.walkthrough: Waves are electromagnetic, not sea or hand waves; 'heartlessly' drops their single middle letter, and 'boxes' puts the rest after the first letter of TALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something according to custom and long practice is doing it as usual.

clue.text: Interminable vocal tirade's empty harangue

indicators.note: without an end, so the last letter of the word for vocal goes

parts.note: oral means spoken, vocal

indicators.note: emptied of its inside, only the outer letters of tirade stay

explanation.surface: An endless spoken rant is a hollow harangue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interminable' trims ORAL to ORA; 'empty' leaves TE from tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver a pompous speech at length is to harangue; both are verbs.

clue.text: King in support employing vessel's English pirate

indicators.note: the result takes in the next pieces, using them inside
the king goes inside the word for support

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar
R, Rex, is king
a vat is a vessel

explanation.surface: A king is propped up by a ship's English buccaneer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R into PIER to make PRIER; 'employing' then takes VATE inside it after PRI.
explanation.definitionFit: A privately owned armed ship licensed to raid enemy shipping, essentially a licensed pirate.

clue.text: Gladiator's axe with handle cut, cut by slice

indicators.note: the shortened words are split open by the next piece
each word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to axe someone is to sack them
to handle something is to use it
a part is a slice or portion

explanation.surface: A gladiator's axe has had its handle shortened and been sliced.
explanation.walkthrough: Axe is the verb, to fire someone, and handle is the verb too; 'cut' docks the last letter of each, and 'cut by' splits the result after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thracian gladiator who led the slave revolt against Rome is the most famous gladiator.

clue.text: Released zombies, perhaps each taken by one

indicators.note: the letters for each are replaced, taken over by the numeral

parts.note: zombies are an example of the walking dead
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone let zombies loose, each grabbed by a single person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' swaps the EA in UNDEAD for I.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie or unfasten something is to release it, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: First woman carrying fine daughter's excited

indicators.note: the name holds the next word inside

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in Genesis
OK means fine
D is short for daughter

explanation.surface: Eve, pregnant with a healthy daughter, is thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' suggests pregnancy, but it only puts the word for fine inside the first woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To call up or arouse a feeling is to excite it; both are past participles here.

clue.text: Musician up in pits in a group

indicators.note: in a down entry the letters read upwards, backwards
the letters lie within the phrase pits in a group

explanation.surface: A musician plays up in the orchestra pit with a group.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'pits in a group' backwards and the answer lies inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: One who plays a keyboard instrument with pipes, as in a church, is a musician.

clue.text: Bond's keen to protect Ian Fleming's ends

indicators.note: the word for keen wraps round the next letters, protecting them

parts.note: to keen is to wail over the dead, to lament

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the phrase Ian Fleming

explanation.surface: James Bond is eager to look after his creator Ian Fleming.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond looks like 007, but it is a tie in the body; keen is the verb, to wail for the dead. 'ends' are the outer letters of Ian Fleming.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of tough tissue binding bone to bone, so a bond in the body.

clue.text: Star rose oddly taking artist's workshops

indicators.note: the odd letters take the artist's name inside
the odd-numbered letters of star rose are kept

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a British artist

explanation.surface: A star rose strangely by taking classes from an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' keeps letters 1, 3, 5 and 7 of star rose; 'taking' puts the artist after the first of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Small study groups meeting for discussion and practice are workshops.

clue.text: Nearly dates male missing gear for bed

parts.note: nigh means nearly

indicators.note: the word for dates lacks the letter for male

parts.note: times are dates, as in fixed times

explanation.surface: Nearly every date, the man is missing kit for bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes M out of TIMES to leave TIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose nightdresses are clothing worn in bed.

clue.text: Bird almost admits sparkling wine's more palatable

indicators.note: the shortened bird lets the wine in
the bird name loses its last letter

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A bird nearly lets in some fizz, finding it nicer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of the bird; 'admits' then lets the wine in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Having more flavour, so nicer to eat: a comparative like more palatable.

clue.text: Pageboy maybe kept holding single Romeo's ring

indicators.note: the word for kept holds the next letters inside

parts.note: had means kept or possessed
I is one, single
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A page boy kept a lone Romeo's ring safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pageboy' sounds like a servant but is a bobbed hairstyle. 'holding' puts IR inside HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageboy is a bobbed hairstyle with the ends curled under, an example of a styled haircut.

clue.text: Following unending drink the French raised excitement

indicators.note: the French article comes after the trimmed drink
both ends of the word for drink are cut off

parts.note: to carouse is to drink freely

indicators.note: in a down entry the French article is read upwards

parts.note: la is French for the

explanation.surface: After endless drinking, the French whipped up some excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unending' trims CAROUSE to AROUS; 'raised' turns LA into AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of being stirred up or stimulated is excitement; both are nouns.

clue.text: Brownie maybe originated with American pinching recipe

indicators.note: the letters pinch the next one between them

parts.note: came, as in came from, means originated
R, from Latin recipe, is the abbreviation on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A brownie recipe originated in America, the clue suggests, with one stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownie looks like a cake or a junior Guide, but it is the Kodak Brownie. 'pinching' puts R inside CAMEA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kodak Brownie was a cheap box camera, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Teeth taking time for fine bites

indicators.note: the word for teeth takes a letter in exchange
the time letter stands in for the fine letter

parts.note: fangs are long pointed teeth
F is short for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Teeth take their time over fine bites.
explanation.walkthrough: Teeth looks like the definition, but it is the starting word; bites is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp flavour or pungency is a bite, as of mustard or lemon.

clue.text: Great aroma nicely circling over lover

indicators.note: turned over, read backwards
the phrase surrounds the letters, encircling them

explanation.surface: A wonderful scent hangs nicely around a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Great aroma nicely' backwards and the answer lies within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian for a woman who is loved, so a female lover or sweetheart.

clue.text: Helps as man's heart has a flutter

indicators.note: the heart of something is its centre, so only the central letter of man is used

parts.note: to have a flutter is to place a small wager, so it bets

explanation.surface: It helps when a man's heart flutters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has a flutter' is British for a small bet, not a racing heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid or encourage someone, often in wrongdoing, is to help them.

clue.text: Firm over bishop with position to secure in …

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
B is the chess notation for bishop

indicators.note: the word for position wraps round the next word, securing it

parts.note: a state is a condition or position

explanation.surface: A chess bishop is firmly held in position, as the clue runs on.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next in the chess theme; 'to secure' wraps the word for position round in.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm in the sense of unyielding, stubbornly refusing to change one's mind.

clue.text: … mean exchange capturing pawn

indicators.note: the word for exchange takes the pawn inside it, as in chess

parts.note: to sell is to exchange for money
P is the chess notation for pawn

explanation.surface: A mean chess trade that wins a pawn, continuing the chess game.
explanation.walkthrough: Mean looks like an adjective, but it is a verb: letters spell out, so mean, a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters spell a word when they make it up, so to spell is to mean or signify.

clue.text: Say Evert scores penultimate point to end set

indicators.note: the tennis player's first name is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: Chris Evert was a champion American tennis player

indicators.note: the next-to-last letter, a compass point, moves to the end of the word

parts.note: tallies are scores

explanation.surface: Chris Evert wins the penultimate point to close out the set.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis scene hides the mechanics: 'Say' gives CRYS for CHRIS; 'penultimate point to end' moves the E of TALLIES to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To set is to harden or solidify, as crystals form when a liquid solidifies.
